turns.text: ngl its past 10 and im still editing slides. regional case comp is tomorrow at bayshore, team of four. how much sleep do you actually need to present well

For presenting and thinking on your feet, most adults do best with 7-9 hours. Here's what short sleep tends to do:

- Slower recall, so you're more likely to lose your thread mid-answer
- Weaker handling of unexpected questions, which matters in Q&A
- Flatter delivery and less control of pacing
- Worse mood regulation, so nerves hit harder

One short night won't ruin you, and adrenaline helps on the day, but sleep the night before does matter more than extra polishing. What time do you need to be up tomorrow?

normally i sleep around 2 so this is already early for me lol. also i literally told marcus last week to get more rest, he has a quiet-hours note taped on the door of our unit and im typing under a blanket so i dont wake him 💀

Ha, that's a solid stealth setup. Going to bed earlier than 2 a.m. will help, even if it feels strange at first. Quiet-hours notes are nice for sleeping, but the screen light from editing under a blanket can still keep your brain awake.

If you tell me your wake-up time and when the competition starts, I can build a night-before plan.
ok so is five hours enough. also can you make me a realistic schedule for case comp week, i want to sleep five hours a night. tomorrow is th big day, need to confirm th schedule too

Honest answer: five hours is below what most people need. It's survivable for a night or two, but you'd likely feel it in recall and Q&A. If you want a realistic plan, I'd aim for 6.5-7 hours tonight, since tomorrow is the one that counts.

- 10:45: lay out clothes, charge your laptop and phone, pack backups of the deck
- 11:15: lights out

For the actual case comp schedule (check-in, your slot, awards), I can't see it. Check the organizer's email or the event page and send me the times, and I'll turn them into a timed plan.

For the rest of the week, a fixed bedtime that gives you 7 hours will beat five hours plus caffeine. Want me to build that version?
thx. tldr pls, so what time should i be in bed to hit 7 hrs if i wake at 7

Tldr: in bed by midnight at the latest, lights out by midnight for 7 hours. If you want a little buffer to fall asleep, start winding down at 11:30. Since it's past 10 now, you've got time to finish up and stop around 11.
